draft.title: Principal Jewish beliefs
card: One God
Jews believe in one God, who created the world and is the only God to be worshipped. This belief is called monotheism.
Covenant
A covenant is a binding agreement. Jews believe God made a covenant with the Jewish people, in which God watches over them and they stay faithful to God.
Commandments
Jews believe that following God's commandments is the way to keep the covenant. Obeying them is a response to God's care and a way to live a holy life.
The three beliefs connect: one God made the covenant, and the commandments are how the people live it out.
draft.remember: One God, one covenant, and commandments followed as part of keeping that covenant.

a.q: What does the Jewish belief in a covenant mean?
opts: A binding agreement between God and the Jewish people
A belief that God takes many forms in the world
A set of laws written by rabbis to guide daily life
A promise made between Jewish people in a community
a.why: A covenant is a binding agreement, and Jews believe God made one with the Jewish people. It is not an agreement among people themselves, because the two sides are God and the people.
a.clue: Think about who the two sides of the agreement are.

b.q: Noah, a Jewish student in Melbourne, says he follows God's commandments because they are part of keeping the covenant. Which belief does this show?
opts: Following commandments is a way of keeping the covenant
Following commandments replaces the need for the covenant
Following commandments shows that God is not one
Following commandments is only needed on special days
b.why: The card links the commandments to the covenant: people live out the agreement by obeying them. The tempting option that commandments replace the covenant is wrong, because they are a way of keeping it, not a substitute.
b.clue: Which belief does Noah say his obedience supports?

a.best: A binding agreement between God and the Jewish people

b.best: Following commandments is a way of keeping the covenant

problems.detail: The stem says Noah follows the commandments 'because they are part of keeping the covenant', and the right option almost repeats it. A student can match the words without knowing the belief.

'One covenant' is misleading. The card speaks of 'a covenant', and Jewish tradition records several covenants, such as with Noah, with Abraham and at Sinai. Point 1 of this chapter names both Abraham's covenant and Sinai.
